skills.name: numberToWords
skills.card:
numberToWords — Spell a number out in English words, the way it is said aloud or written on a cheque.
  needs: value: number
  optional: style: string, currency: string
  e.g. "write 1234 in words" → {"value":1234}

value.label: number
value.prompt: Which number should I write out?

examples: write 105.50 as words for a cheque

skills.name: columnMath

operation.label: operation
operation.prompt: Sum, average, min, max or count?

examples: highest value in the score column
sum a column with a blank cell in it
how many rows have a value in name

skills.name: filterRows

column.label: column
column.prompt: Which column should I filter on?

value.label: compare to
value.prompt: What should I compare it to?

examples: keep only rows where amount is over 100
show me just the North region rows
drop everything at or below zero

skills.name: formatJson
skills.card:
formatJson — Tidy JSON into readable indented form, or squash it onto one line.
  needs: text: string
  optional: style: string, indent: integer, sortKeys: boolean
  e.g. "pretty print this json" → {"text":"{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}"}
examples: tidy the json and sort the keys
tidy this json so a person can read it

skills.name: groupBy
skills.card:
groupBy — Total or average rows per category, grouped by a shared value.
  needs: table: object, column: string
  optional: aggregate: string, operation: string
  e.g. "group these rows by region and sum the amounts" → {"table":{"headers":["region","amount"],"rows":[{"region":"north","amount":120},{"region":"south","amount":80},{"region":"north","amount":200}]},"column":"region","aggregate":"amount","operation":"sum"}

column.label: group by column
column.prompt: Which column should I group by?

aggregate.label: value column
aggregate.description: the column to aggregate — required for anything other than count

examples: group these rows by region and sum the amounts
count the rows in each category
find the highest price in each shop
group by status when every row is the same
sum the points for each team in this table
how many rows fall under each status

skills.name: parseCsv
skills.card:
parseCsv — Read CSV text into rows and columns, detecting the header line.
  needs: text: string
  optional: delimiter: string, hasHeader: boolean
  e.g. "parse this csv: name,amount
Ana,120
Bo,80" → {"text":"name,amount\nAna,120\nBo,80"}

text.label: csv
text.prompt: Which CSV text should I read?

examples:
parse this csv: name,amount
Ana,120
Bo,80
read a csv with a quoted comma
parse csv without a header row
read three columns of sales data

skills.name: pivotRows
skills.card:
pivotRows — Cross-tabulate one column against another into a grid of cells.
  needs: table: object, rowColumn: string, columnColumn: string
  optional: valueColumn: string, operation: string
  e.g. "pivot amount by region and quarter" → {"table":{"headers":["region","quarter","amount"],"rows":[{"region":"north","quarter":"Q1","amount":10},{"region":"north","quarter":"Q2","amount":20},{"region":"south","quarter":"Q1","amount":30}]},"rowColumn":"region","columnColumn":"quarter","valueColumn":"amount","operation":"sum"}

rowColumn.label: rows from column
rowColumn.prompt: Which column should become the rows?

columnColumn.label: columns from column
columnColumn.prompt: Which column should become the columns?

valueColumn.label: value column
valueColumn.description: the column to aggregate - required for anything other than count

examples: pivot amount by region and quarter
count rows by day and type
average sales by store and month
highest points by team and round

skills.name: sortObjectKeys
skills.card:
sortObjectKeys — Sort the keys of a JSON object alphabetically, all the way down.
  needs: json: string
  optional: direction: string, indent: integer
  e.g. "sort the keys in this json" → {"json":"{\"b\":2,\"a\":1}"}
examples: sort the keys in this json
sort json whose keys are already in order
alphabetise the keys in this json object

skills.name: sortRows
skills.card:
sortRows — Reorder the rows of a table by a column, changing nothing else.
  needs: table: object, column: string
  optional: direction: string, then: string
  e.g. "sort by amount, biggest first" → {"table":{"headers":["name","amount"],"rows":[{"name":"Ana","amount":120},{"name":"Bo","amount":80},{"name":"Cy","amount":200}]},"column":"amount","direction":"descending"}

column.label: sort by column
column.prompt: Which column should I sort by?

then.label: then by column
then.description: a second column, used to break ties

examples: order by region then by q1

skills.name: toCsv
skills.card:
toCsv — Turn rows and columns back into CSV text, quoting anything that needs it.
  needs: table: object
  optional: delimiter: string, includeHeader: boolean
  e.g. "turn this table back into csv" → {"table":{"headers":["name","amount"],"rows":[{"name":"Ana","amount":120},{"name":"Bo","amount":80}]}}

table.label: table
table.prompt: Which table should I write out?

examples: turn this table back into csv
write this out as csv, quoting the comma
write a cell containing a quote mark

skills.name: toMarkdownTable
skills.card:
toMarkdownTable — Draw rows and columns out as a markdown table, pipes and all.
  needs: table: object
  optional: align: string
  e.g. "make a markdown table from this data" → {"table":{"headers":["name","amount"],"rows":[{"name":"Ana","amount":120},{"name":"Bo","amount":80}]}}
examples: make a markdown table from this data
format as a right-aligned markdown table
markdown table with a pipe in a cell
markdown table with an empty cell

skills.name: addDuration

from.label: start date
from.prompt: Which date should I start from?

amount.label: how many
amount.prompt: How many should I add? (use a negative number to go back)

skills.name: dateRangeList
skills.card:
dateRangeList — List every date between two dates, optionally stepping by weeks or months.
  needs: from: string, to: string
  optional: step: integer, unit: string, weekdaysOnly: boolean
  e.g. "list the dates from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-05" → {"from":"2026-09-01","to":"2026-09-05"}
examples: the first of each month from january to april 2026

skills.name: durationToText
skills.card:
durationToText — Turn a raw number of seconds into readable words like "1h 30m".
  needs: seconds: number
  optional: style: string, maxUnits: integer
  e.g. "what is 5400 seconds as a duration" → {"seconds":5400}
examples: what is 5400 seconds as a duration
how long is 90 seconds in words

skills.name: expandRecurrence
skills.card:
expandRecurrence — List the dates a repeating schedule falls on — the first Thursday monthly, every fortnight, every 90 days.
  needs: start: string
  optional: every: string, interval: integer, count: integer, until: string
  e.g. "every fortnight from 2026-09-07, eight times" → {"start":"2026-09-07","every":"week","interval":2,"count":8}

start.label: start date
start.prompt: What date does it start on?

count.label: how many dates
count.description: defaults to 10 without an end date

examples: the 1st of every month for six months from 2026-10-01
my birthday every year from 2026-03-09, four times

skills.name: nextWeekday
skills.card:
nextWeekday — Find the date of the next Monday, Tuesday and so on — or the most recent one.
  needs: weekday: string
  optional: direction: string, from: string
  e.g. "when is next tuesday" → {"weekday":"Tuesday"}
examples: what date is the next friday

skills.name: unixToIso
skills.card:
unixToIso — Turn a Unix timestamp into a readable date and time.
  needs: unix: number
  optional: unit: string
  e.g. "what date is unix timestamp 1788255000" → {"unix":1788255000}

skills.name: generatePalette
skills.card:
generatePalette — Build a colour palette around a base colour — analogous, triadic, complementary or tints and shades.
  needs: color: string
  optional: scheme: string, count: integer
  e.g. "build an analogous palette from #2C6E8C" → {"color":"#2C6E8C"}

color.label: base colour
color.prompt: Which colour should the palette be built around?

count.label: colours (tints/shades)
count.description: only used for tints and shades

skills.name: generateRandomString
examples: generate a random code people can read out
a strong random password with symbols

skills.name: hashText
skills.card:
hashText — Work out the SHA hash of a piece of text.
  needs: text: string
  optional: algorithm: string
  e.g. "sha256 of hello" → {"text":"hello"}

skills.name: hexEncode
skills.card:
hexEncode — Write text out as hexadecimal byte values.
  needs: text: string
  optional: separator: string, uppercase: boolean
  e.g. "hex encode Pigeon" → {"text":"Pigeon"}
examples: hex encode with spaces between bytes

skills.name: urlEncode
skills.card:
urlEncode — Percent-escape text so it survives inside a web address.
  needs: text: string
  optional: scope: string
  e.g. "url encode "hello world"" → {"text":"hello world"}
examples: encode this for a query string
encode a whole url leaving the slashes
encode text that needs no encoding
make this text safe for a url query: café au lait
percent encode this for a web address: a&b=c

skills.name: splitBill
skills.card:
splitBill — Add a tip to a bill and split it between people, to the exact penny.
  needs: bill: number
  optional: tipPercent: number, people: integer, currency: string
  e.g. "split a 84.50 bill four ways with 15% tip" → {"bill":84.5,"tipPercent":15,"people":4}
examples: split a 84.50 bill four ways with 15% tip
dinner was 45.60, 12.5 percent tip, two people
bill of 200 split 8 ways with 10% service

skills.name: fileSizeHuman
skills.card:
fileSizeHuman — Turn a number of bytes into a readable file size like 1.4 MB.
  needs: bytes: number
  optional: base: string, decimals: integer
  e.g. "how big is 1500000 bytes" → {"bytes":1500000}
examples: make 1073741824 bytes readable in binary units
what is 512 bytes as a file size
how big is an empty file

skills.name: compoundInterest
skills.card:
compoundInterest — Grow a sum year on year, with each year’s interest earning interest too.
  needs: principal: number, rate: number, years: number
  optional: frequency: string, contribution: number
  e.g. "what does 1000 grow to at 5% for 10 years" → {"principal":1000,"rate":5,"years":10}

principal.label: starting amount
principal.prompt: How much is the starting amount?

rate.label: annual rate %
rate.prompt: What annual interest rate, as a percentage?

examples: what does 1000 grow to at 5% for 10 years
save 200 a month at 6% for 20 years

skills.name: generateCalendarGrid
skills.card:
generateCalendarGrid — Draw a month out as a printable calendar grid of weeks.
  needs: year: integer, month: integer
  optional: startOn: string
  e.g. "show me a calendar grid for September 2026" → {"year":2026,"month":9}

month.label: month
month.prompt: Which month, as a number from 1 to 12?

examples: show me a calendar grid for September 2026
calendar starting on Sunday for September 2026
show february 2027 as a grid of weeks
lay out march 2027 week by week
